jurisdiction.name: World Health Organization
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: WHO has issued global guidance on the ethics and governance of AI in health (2021), extended in 2024–2025 to large multi-modal (generative) models, and a set of regulatory considerations for AI in health (2023). It has also published a framework for generating evidence on AI-based medical devices. The World Health Assembly has not adopted a resolution dedicated to AI; AI governance was discussed in 2026 under an agenda item on data, digital health and AI.

instruments.official_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
instruments.english_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance
instruments.summary: WHO guidance on artificial intelligence in health. It sets out six consensus principles (protect autonomy; promote well-being, safety and the public interest; ensure transparency, explainability and intelligibility; foster responsibility and accountability; ensure inclusiveness and equity; promote responsive and sustainable AI) and recommendations for governments, developers and providers on governance, liability, data protection and oversight of AI used in health.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization on 28 June 2021.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 28 June 2021 printed on WHO publication page (ISBN 9789240029200). Executive summary is a separate item (9789240037403), not recorded separately. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 28 June 2021 and 'six consensus principles' confirmed.; 'Non-binding' and 'first global guidance' not stated on the page.

instruments.official_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
instruments.english_title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: Guidance on large multi-modal models
instruments.summary: Guidance applying WHO's AI ethics principles to large multi-modal models (generative AI) in health. It describes uses in diagnosis, patient-guided use, clerical tasks, education and research, sets out risks, and gives over 40 recommendations for governments, developers and providers across the design, development and deployment of such models, including regulation, audits, impact assessments and liability.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization; the publication page is dated 25 March 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: WHO publication page (ISBN 9789240084759) prints 25 March 2025. The guidance was first released on 18 January 2024 (per WHO news release, not re-verified); the page now carries the 2025 version only, so the printed 2025 date is used. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title and 25 March 2025 date confirmed on the WHO page; recommendation count and audiences not on the landing page (taken as from the PDF).; 'Non-binding' not stated.

instruments.official_title: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health
instruments.english_title: Regulatory considerations on artificial intelligence for health
instruments.summary: Sets out key regulatory considerations for AI systems in health for regulators, developers and manufacturers, grouped under documentation and transparency, risk management and life-cycle approach, intended use and analytical and clinical validation, data quality, privacy and data protection, and engagement and collaboration among regulators, patients, providers and industry.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization on 19 October 2023 as a high-level overview of considerations; WHO states it is not intended as guidance, as a regulatory framework or policy.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 19 October 2023 printed on WHO publication page. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 19 Oct 2023 and audiences confirmed. Page states the overview is 'not intended as guidance, as a regulatory framework or policy'.

instruments.official_title: Generating Evidence for Artificial Intelligence Based Medical Devices: A Framework for Training Validation and Evaluation
instruments.english_title: Generating evidence for artificial intelligence-based medical devices: a framework for training, validation and evaluation
instruments.summary: Framework for developers, regulators and health authorities on generating clinical and technical evidence for AI-based medical devices across their life cycle, covering data management, model training, validation and evaluation, and post-market monitoring.
instruments.current_status: Published by the World Health Organization on 17 November 2021.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 17 November 2021 printed on WHO publication page (ISBN 9789240038462). Developed with the ITU/WHO Focus Group on AI for Health; issued in WHO's name. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 17 Nov 2021 and content confirmed (uses cervical cancer screening as use case).; 'Non-binding' not stated.

leads.title: Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 (endorsed by WHA73 in 2020; extended to 2027 by WHA78 in 2025)
leads.note: Digital health strategy; AI is one of several technologies covered rather than a dedicated section. PDF text could not be checked for an AI-specific commitment.

leads.title: EB158/19 Harmonization of regulatory approaches, governance and standards for data, digital health and artificial intelligence in the health sector
leads.note: Secretariat report to the Executive Board (2026) and WHA79 agenda item 12.10; no resolution on AI was adopted at WHA79 (May 2026). A new digital health strategy 2028–2033 is in preparation for WHA80 (2027).

leads.title: Artificial intelligence-related health research: ethics review and oversight (21 July 2026)
leads.note: Classified by WHO as a report, not guidance; offers non-exhaustive considerations for research ethics committees.

membership_note: WHO has 194 Member States, including the Cook Islands and Niue; Liechtenstein is not a member. WHO records that the United States notified its withdrawal effective 22 January 2026, subject to consideration by WHO's governing bodies.

members_source.comment: WHO countries page states 194 Member States and lists them (all UN Member States except Liechtenstein, plus Cook Islands and Niue). A footnote records the United States' notice of withdrawal with an effective date of 22 January 2026, pending consideration by WHO governing bodies. Read 2026-10-21.
